core_obligations: The author transfers controllability of constant targets to polynomial targets by an induction adapted to the delay endpoint operator, then uses density for general approximate controllability. Exact controllability in the original two-state/two-delay scalar-input setting needs a separate adjoint spectral/Fourier obstruction argument. Both constant-target regimes are retained as one object.

dedup.scope: Same-source public1918 characterizes approximate versus exact controllability for canonical two-state systems with irrational delays (MainTheo22). Selected Section5 constant-target equivalence is an additional main problem: general finite-dimensional approximate equivalence via polynomial induction, and exact equivalence only for the original two-state/two-delay scalar-input systems. The canonical classification remains support, not re-counted; the two constant-target regimes form one object.
